name: Samaria Ancient
overview: Samaria, named after Shemer who owned the hill on which it was built, was established by King Omri as a significant city in Israel (1 Kings 16:24). It was situated in a mountainous region, which Joshua encouraged the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh to possess despite the strength of their enemies (Joshua 17:17-18). Scripture reveals Samaria as a center of idolatry and corruption, with prophetic declarations against its high places and altars that would inevitably come to pass (1 Kings 13:32). The city also served as a royal burial place, highlighting its importance in Israel’s history (1 Kings 16:28).
